alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition Fe-31Mn-9Al-1C-0.45Nb-0.45Mo-0.45W (wt%). The exact measured content (wt%) was: Mn 30.9, Al 8.7, C 0.9, Nb 0.45, Mo 0.45, W 0.43, Fe balance. The conclusions section re-states the composition as Fe-31Mn-9Al-0.9C-0.45Nb-0.45Mo-0.45W (wt%). Measured density 6.82 g/cm3 (~13% reduction vs pure iron). The same steel composition was used for all hot-rolling reductions.
alloys.description: A single fully austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel produced by high-frequency vacuum induction melting and hot forging; investigated to enhance overall mechanical properties (strength, ductility, toughness) via increasing hot-rolling reduction.

source.reason: The paper studies one single steel; the nominal composition is given in Section 2.1 as Fe-31Mn-9Al-1C-0.45Nb-0.45Mo-0.45W (wt%) with exact measured contents, and the Introduction/abstract describe it as a Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic low-density steel. All HR samples share this identical composition ('the chemical composition of the three investigated sample was the same'), so only one alloy entity is defined.

paper.paper_scope: Investigates how increasing the hot-rolling reduction (45%, 68%, 82%) affects the microstructure evolution, mechanical properties, strengthening mechanisms, and three-staged strain-hardening behavior of a single Fe-31Mn-9Al-1C-0.45Nb-0.45Mo-0.45W austenitic low-density steel.
paper.title: Enhanced mechanical properties of a Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic low-density steel by increasing hot-rolling reduction

processes.description: Hot-forged billet reheated at 1150 °C and hot-rolled to a 45% reduction (4 passes, plate thickness 60 mm), then water quenched to room temperature.
processes.process_name: Hot-rolled to 45% reduction then water quenched
processes.processes_notes: All three rolling states share the same prior processing (1150 °C hot forging and 1150 °C reheating) and the same water-quench finish; they differ only in the rolling reduction (45%, 68%, 82%) and number of passes (4, 6, 9).

Combination of the single Fe-31Mn-9Al-1C-0.45Nb-0.45Mo-0.45W alloy with the 45% hot-rolling reduction process; explicitly denoted HR45 and reported with grain size 45.11 µm, YS 480 MPa, UTS 861 MPa, TE 60%.
Combination of the single alloy with the 68% hot-rolling reduction process; explicitly denoted HR68 and reported with grain size 27.02 µm, YS 577 MPa, UTS 922 MPa, TE 57%.
Combination of the single alloy with the 82% hot-rolling reduction process; explicitly denoted HR82 and reported with grain size 18.80 µm, YS 648 MPa, UTS 976 MPa, TE 50%.

unmapped_findings: The measured density of the investigated steel is 6.82 g/cm3 (Archimedes' principle), corresponding to ~13% density reduction relative to pure iron.
The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the present steel was calculated to be ~73 mJ/m2 based on the Olson-Cohen thermodynamic model.

Two kinds of precipitates were present: micron- and submicron-sized (Nb,Mo,W)C MC-type complex carbides (FCC, lattice parameter 4.36 Å) and nano-sized (Fe,Mn)3AlCx κ-carbides with an L′12-type ordered structure formed during water quenching (without aging); the κ-carbide volume fraction was ~3.5%, 3.3%, and 3.9% for HR45, HR68, and HR82, respectively.

The three investigated samples exhibited a three-staged strain-hardening behavior governed by the transition of planar deformation substructures (slip bands → microbands), with the slip band spacing saturating at ~50 nm.
